claims.statement: The live editor surface is composed of three mounted React components (FileBrowser, FileEditor, FileDiffViewer) plus a standalone Terminal component, all of which call a dedicated set of server routes under app/api/tasks/[taskId]/. All twelve editor routes share the same preamble: getServerSession, ownership scoping by userId with isNull(deletedAt), require task.sandboxId, then look the sandbox up via getSandbox(taskId) ?? Sandbox.get({ sandboxId, teamId, projectId, token }).

The editor surface exposes four view modes ('remote', 'local', 'all', 'all-local') that toggle between GitHub-sourced data and in-sandbox data; only 'remote' and 'local' produce a DiffFile rendered by DiffView, while 'all' and 'all-local' delegate to FileEditor for plain text render.

FileBrowser state is held in a per-task Jotai atom (lib/atoms/file-browser.ts) with one ViewModeData slot per mode; the browser renders an AlertDialog with a Start Sandbox button when the server responds with a 410 Gone or 'Sandbox is not running' error.

FileEditor wraps @monaco-editor/react with two Vercel/Geist themes, disables Monaco's TypeScript semantic diagnostics (noSemanticValidation: true) so the sandbox LSP remains authoritative, registers Cmd/Ctrl+S for save via /api/tasks/:taskId/save-file, and rewires F12 and Cmd/Ctrl+Click to call /api/tasks/:taskId/lsp for Go-to-Definition; cross-file results call onOpenFile(filePath, lineNumber).

The save-file route writes through a base64-encoded pipe (sh -c "echo '<base64>' | base64 -d > '<escaped-filename>'") with the filename shell-escaped, avoiding heredoc injection vulnerabilities from content containing sequences like 'EOF'; the autocomplete route shell-escapes the directory argument with the same '\\'' trick when running ls -1ap in the sandbox.

The terminal component POSTs each user command to /api/tasks/:taskId/terminal (sh -c <command> in PROJECT_DIR) and POSTs pwd to the same endpoint after a successful cd to refresh its cached cwd; Tab calls /api/tasks/:taskId/autocomplete which runs ls -1ap in the sandbox and returns case-insensitive prefix matches with isDirectory derived from the trailing slash.

The LSP route declares runtime='nodejs' and maxDuration=60; its textDocument/definition case writes a .lsp-helper.mjs into the sandbox that uses ts.createLanguageService with a ts.parseJsonConfigFileContent host (walking up from process.cwd() to find tsconfig.json), runs it with node, parses JSON.stringify from stdout, removes the helper, and returns definitions converted from 0-indexed LSP coordinates. The textDocument/hover and textDocument/completion cases are stubs returning empty results; the vscode-jsonrpc + typescript-language-server + ws dependencies are declared in package.json for the planned bridge.

The diff route's default (PR) mode uses PR base.sha and head.sha when task.prNumber is set so the diff is anchored to PR creation time rather than current main; when the PR is merged, the route writes prMergeCommitSha back to the tasks row if it was empty. Files mode (mode=all) uses git.getTree recursive on task.branchName via Octokit, while files mode mode=all-local runs find inside the sandbox excluding .git, node_modules, .next, dist, build, and .vercel and joins the result with git status to color entries.

FileBrowser right-click actions funnel file-system mutations through dedicated routes: create-file (mkdir -p + touch), create-folder (mkdir -p), delete-file (rm), file-operation (cp -r or mv via the operation field), and discard-file-changes (git ls-files probe followed by git checkout HEAD -- <path> for tracked files or rm for untracked files).

FileDiffViewer renders the unified DiffView from @git-diff-view/react with DiffModeEnum.Unified, using generateDiffFile from @git-diff-view/file; both file-content and diff routes return early with isBinary: true for non-image binaries, and image files come back with isBase64: true so the viewer can wrap them in a data:<mime>;base64,... URL whose mime is derived from the extension (including image/svg+xml and image/x-icon).

All editor routes assume the task is in keepAlive mode because every route gates on task.sandboxId being non-null; when Sandbox.get throws (sandbox expired or never reachable), file routes return 500 to the client and the browser renders the 'Sandbox is not running' alert with a Start Sandbox button. Only the files route proactively clears tasks.sandboxId and tasks.sandboxUrl when the SDK reports a 410 Gone; the other editor routes leave cleanup to the next start-sandbox call.
